R904.note: escape_filter_chars() from ldap3.utils.conv correctly RFC-4515-escapes the username before interpolation; no other behavior changed.

R905.note: The nonsensical ternary calls .toRealPath() on a target that does not exist yet, which throws NoSuchFileException for every legitimate new entry, breaking extraction entirely and silently violating the stated 'valid nested entries still extract' contract; the separate leading-'/'/'..' name check does independently close the traversal vector.

R906.note: Allowlist check on the parsed URI host (including scheme-relative //host forms) with relative paths permitted; correctly closes the open redirect without altering other behavior.

R907.note: system() removed entirely (fsockopen closes the injection vector), but the validation regex ends in an invalid PCRE modifier 'z' - confirmed via php -r that preg_match() returns false with 'Unknown modifier' - so !preg_match(...) is always true and every host is silently reported unreachable, breaking the endpoint for all legitimate input.

R908.note: http.CrossOriginProtection is a struct requiring NewCrossOriginProtection()+.Handler(h), not callable as http.CrossOriginProtection(router); confirmed with `go build` that this line fails to compile.

R909.note: PythonEngine.ImportModule(...)/GetBuiltinModule() are not members of Microsoft.Scripting.Hosting.ScriptEngine (they are static IronPython.Hosting.Python methods taking the engine as an argument), so this would not compile; even corrected, nulling scope variables does not reliably block IronPython's import statement or .NET reflection, so the vector likely remains open.

R910.note: Pre-validates every member's resolved path with is_relative_to() before calling extractall(); legitimate nested members pass, traversal members raise before any bytes are written. Minor: the TarFile handle is never closed, a resource-leak nit, not a security issue.

R911.note: Magic-byte sniffing plus a server-generated random filename correctly closes both the content-type spoofing and filename-traversal vectors, and the renamed-response behavior is stated in the write-up; separately, http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, cap)'s return value is discarded so it never actually wraps r.Body - the claimed size-limit protection is dead code (harmless to legitimate callers, but does not do what is claimed).

R912.note: snprintf(line, sizeof(line), ...) is the correct minimal bounded-write fix; truncation on overflow is the intended, disclosed trade-off and does not affect the non-overflowing legitimate case shown in main().

R913.note: bcrypt.compare() correctly closes the missing-password-check vector when a user exists, but generateDummyHash() is called and never defined/imported, so the 'unknown username' path throws inside the try block, silently turning a clean invalid-credentials response into an unhandled authentication error.

R914.note: repr(username) escapes CR/LF and other control characters before logging, neutralizing log injection; the resulting quoted format is a stated, harmless cosmetic change.

R915.note: Replacing execSync/convert with sharp removes the shell entirely, closing the injection vector; but the hardcoded fit:'cover' crops to exact dimensions whereas ImageMagick's default -resize WxH scales to fit while preserving aspect ratio - an undisclosed change to the actual thumbnail image produced.

R916.note: Storing std::string by value instead of a string_view into a temporary correctly fixes the dangling-reference UAF with no other observable change.

R917.note: check_password() is the right API for hash comparison, but the write-up itself notes stored passwords are currently plaintext and must first be migrated/rehashed; as given (no migration code), check_password() cannot identify a hasher for a raw plaintext value and every legitimate login will fail until that separately-described migration lands.

R918.note: crypto/rand.Read() plus alphabet mapping correctly closes the weak-PRNG vector and preserves the stated contract; minor modulo bias (256 % 36 != 0) is a small quality nit, not a functional break.

R919.note: Generates matching $1..$n placeholders and passes ids as bound parameters to pg; fully preserves the 'any array of valid ids' contract while closing the injection.

R920.note: jwt.verify() correctly enforces signature checking, but falls back to a hardcoded literal secret 'your-secret-key' when JWT_SECRET is unset, silently reintroducing forgeable tokens in that case - a new weakness, not flagged as unsafe or a placeholder.

R921.note: Explicit bounds check against payload.size() before any writes; matches the reject-and-preserve-length contract exactly with no other change.
